title: The City of London and Brexit 10 Years On
summary: Abstract Ten years after the Brexit referendum, the impact of Brexit on the City of London remains contested. Conventional proposals for a single circulating currency undermine national central bank autonomy, while purely bilateral local-currency trading mechanisms create structural balance-of-payments imbalances and unconvertible currency surpluses. This paper presents the BRICS Synthetic Clearing Bridge (BSCB), a multilateral, non-circulating digital clearing architecture. The framework combines: 1. An idiosyncratic emergency protocol featuring a targeted 30-day pre-crisis price freeze rule on relief commodities. 5. An automated Trade-Recovery Conduit to settle structural synthetic debits via consignment export arbitrage, backed by post-sunset sovereign rollover rights. 6. summary: Political economy theory expects politicians to use budget deficits to engineer an election-timed boom, known as the political business cycle. We challenge and contextualize this view by incorporating the financial constraints faced by governments into an electoral framework.
